National rural seats hold firm ahead of election

Hugh Stringleman
October 5, 2026
Total

But latest polling shows that may not be enough to put coalition government back in power on November 7.
Reading Time: 3 minutes

Rural electorates will stay loyal to National in the November 7 general election but that may not be enough to ensure the return of the coalition government.

This is the gist of current polling, which shows the National Party could lose up to 10 electorates where its party vote majorities in 2023 were up to 8% better than in 2020.

Seven of those electorates are in the cities and three are predominately rural.

In 2023 National’s share of the vote improved from 25.5% to 38% and the swing against Labour saw it fall from 50% to 27%.

Current opinion polls put National around 30%, an erosion of 8%, while Labour is fixed on 27%.

On the surface, National’s loss of support has gone to the medium parties – ACT, NZ First, Green and Opportunity.

In the Parliament National has 48 MPs, 43 of whom represent electorates.

Should its party vote fall to 30% evenly across the country the loss of 10 MPs would occur in seven urban electorates and only three rural seats – West Coast-Tasman, Northland and Ōtaki.

The National electorates at most risk are (in order of their 2023 margins) Banks Peninsula 396 votes, New Lynn 1013, West Coast-Tasman 1017, Hutt South 1332, Mt Roskill 1564, Maungakiekie 4617, Hamilton East 5060, Hamilton West 6488, Northland 6087, Ōtaki 6271.

In West Coast-Tasman Maureen Pugh achieved an 8% increase on her 2020 votes, while Labour’s agriculture minister, Damien O’Connor, fell by 23%. Neither are contesting that electorate this time around.

National has a well-known candidate in Katie Milne, former Federated Farmers national president and Westland dairy farmer, up against Labour’s North Canterbury-based teacher Rory Paterson, a former deputy principal in Greymouth.

O’Connor has moved to Waitaki electorate to contest his 12th general election, where he will challenge sitting MP and former senior Federated Farmers official Miles Anderson for National and broadcaster and local government councillor Michael Laws for NZ First.

National’s grip on Northland and Ōtaki relies on the personal appeal and hard work of farmer Grant McCallum in the north and former Royal NZ Air Force pilot Tim Costley in Ōtaki.

Elsewhere in the country, National has eight current MPs defending their rural electorates – Dana Kirkpatrick, East Coast; Barbara Kuriger, Taranaki-King Country; Catherine Wedd, Tukituki; Suze Redmayne, Rangitīkei; Stuart Smith, Kaikoura; James Meager, Rangitata; Nicola Grigg, Selwyn; and Joseph Mooney, Southland. 

12 Regional seats to watch

• Northland – Grant McCallum, first-term National MP; Shane Jones, deputy leader of NZ First and List MP; Davina Smolders, ACT List candidate; and Mike Finlayson, Green Party.

• East Coast – Dana Kirkpatrick, first-term National MP; Jo Luxton, Labour List MP; and Darrin Hawkes, ACT.

• Taranaki-King Country – Barbara Kuriger, National MP; Lee Smith, NZ First candidate and Groundswell spokesperson; and Ivana Jovicic, ACT.

• Tukituki – Catherine Wedd, first-term National MP; Taine Randell, NZ First candidate and former All Blacks captain: and Rob Douglas, ACT.

• Rangitīkei – Suze Redmayne, first-term National MP; Andrew Hoggard, ACT List MP and former Federated Farmers president; and Steve Gibson, NZ First candidate, district councillor.

• West Coast Tasman – Katie Milne, National candidate and former Federated Farmers president; Rory Paterson, Labour candidate; Jamie Cliene, NZ First and former mayor of Buller District; and Janelle Hocking, ACT candidate.

• Kaikoura – Stuart Smith, National MP; Jamie Arbuckle, NZ First List MP; and Tom Spooner, ACT.

• Rangitata – James Meager, first-term National MP, Isaac Nicolson, NZ First; and Aaron Allred, ACT.

• Selwyn – Nicola Grigg, National MP; Iain Murray, ACT; and Elizabeth Mundt, NZ First district councillor. 

• Waitaki – Miles Anderson, first-term National MP; Damien O’Connor, 11-term Labour MP; Michael Laws, NZ First local government councillor; and Sean Beamish, ACT.

• Taieri – Ingrid Leary, Labour MP; Mark Patterson, NZ First List MP; and Matthew French, National.

• Southland – Joseph Mooney, first-term National MP; Todd Stephenson, ACT List MP; Jason Herrick, NZ First and Southland Federated Farmers president.
